reply_text:
㊥ (historical count) Across the 1,249 operator turns in the live store, from 22 September to now, 286 turns would show red: 23%, with 400 red phrases in all. The share is fairly steady, about a quarter of your turns on busy days. On 30 September and 1 October, 56 of 218 and 55 of 197 turns had red. Most often:

| Node | Phrases |
|---|---:|
| GRAIN-GATE | 38 |
| R20 | 36 |
| R4 | 34 |
| R5 | 31 |
| R13 | 31 |
| R17 | 28 |
| R6 | 27 |
| R2 | 26 |

The rarest are R3 (9) and CTAU-CLASS (8). The phrases that fire most are "worth" (R5) and "stop" (R20), 19 each, then "before we" (R13) 18, "here is" (R2) 15, "either … or" (R6) 13, and "rule" (GRAIN-GATE) 12.

🖖 (what *should* turn red) The idea is that a phrase turns red when it names a step of the War Machine's loop that you're doing yourself, and it isn't one of the phrases that mark how you're addressing the agent. The intent tells you what kind of move the turn makes. The red tells you which requirement of a working control loop the turn touches. Some examples from the current vocabulary:

| Step | Examples | What you're doing |
|---|---|---|
| R13, looking ahead | "before we", "sequence", "plan ahead" | ordering steps ahead of time |
| R5, worth it | "worth", "worth exploring" | weighing value against information |
| GRAIN-GATE, what may be done | "rule", "as long as", "do not" | restricting what's allowed |
| R20, alarm | "stop", "annoying" | signalling something is wrong |
| R11, budget | "spend", "tokens" | managing a shared resource |
| R10, runs without you | "overnight" | scheduling work you won't trigger |
| R17, learning from use | "that worked", "merge" | changing what gets used, based on what worked |
| R1, what you hold true | "pretty sure", "my sense" | stating a belief |

㊟ (the honest caveat) That's the intention, not a guarantee. The list came from agents' reading of your turns plus the machine narrative, and it's only been checked statistically, at roughly twice chance against the turn bids. Some red will be wrong: "stop" in "the bus stop", say, or "rule" used loosely. The historical count is useful to inspect: it shows which words carry the volume, and you can tell me which ones look wrong to you.

🖖 (new test sentence) The earlier example used phrases that are now intent cues. This one avoids them:

> Before we run it overnight, I'm pretty sure either the cache or the index will spend most of the tokens; that worked last time, so it's worth a health check.

These should go red: "Before we" (R13), "overnight" (R10), "pretty sure" (R1), "either … or" (R6), "spend" and "tokens" (R11), "that worked" (R17), "worth" (R5) and "health check" (R20).
